verdict: M241r2 repairs the concrete M249 failures for the tested standalone eight-lane subset. Independent exact-SHA VCS recompilation and simulation reproduce the formal run's assertion report byte-for-byte. Fixed 1/2/3-cycle modes and a deterministic varying 1-to-3-cycle mode pass with request, response, commit and abort stalls. Each mode replays 126 independently decoded real descriptors, 504 destination writes and 4,032 signed lane checks with zero mismatch; stale weight-epoch and accumulator-payload responses have zero accepts; overflow has commit_valid=0, commit_accept=0 and writes=0, discards two accepted younger tokens, then reset recovery commits once. Loader binding, window/epoch/payload cache identity, lazy valid, same-address interlock, zero forwarding payload and no M149 instance are structurally present. An independent review-only SVA overlay closes the production SVA's missing response-tag-stability check and passes one real weight and one real accumulator response-stall cover. Two milestone claims require correction: the fourth mode is not random because the TB contains no RNG and different seeds produce identical reports; and four bounded modes do not by themselves prove arbitrary finite latency. The admitted result is a bounded standalone protocol repair, not full96, a complete trace, DC/STA, energy, measured speedup, physical speedup, system speedup, paper PPA or headline.

findings.title: The fourth latency mode is deterministic, not randomized
findings.evidence: The TB contains zero $urandom calls. Weight/accumulator latency is 1+(accepted_request_count%3), while request and launch stalls use cycle_count modulo constants. Replays with seeds 241220260825 and 25920260825 produce byte-identical assertion reports and identical PASS lines.
findings.required_fix: Rename the mode to deterministic varying 1-to-3, or add independently seeded randomized latency/stall sequences plus seed receipts before claiming random coverage.

findings.title: Production SVA does not hold the complete response identity stable under stall
findings.evidence: Production assertions hold response bank_valid and every data lane stable, but omit sequence/operator/partition/window/epoch/payload/order/source/half from weight response stability and omit sequence/window/epoch/payload/order from accumulator response stability. The M259 review overlay adds these properties and passes one covered stall for each response.
findings.required_fix: Promote the M259 complete-tag stability properties into the production SVA and reseal the formal exact run.

findings.title: Arbitrary finite response latency is over-admitted
findings.evidence: Exact VCS tests fixed 1/2/3 and one deterministic varying 1-to-3 schedule. The RTL is structurally wait-state elastic, but no formal liveness/safety proof or wider latency sweep establishes every arbitrary finite latency and stall composition.
findings.required_fix: Restrict admission to tested bounded elasticity, or add formal assumptions/proofs and a broader latency/backpressure sweep.

findings.title: The real workload is an eight-lane no-tail subset
findings.evidence: All 126 descriptors are full4, cover only 8 of 96 lanes, one sample/operator/partition/window, and contain no natural tail descriptors.
findings.required_fix: Extend to full96 and a complete finite trace with tails and multiple contexts before performance or complete-workload claims.

findings.title: The directed tag-corruption matrix is sparse
findings.evidence: The stale weight attack flips epoch, stale accumulator attack flips payload ID, and loader attack flips payload ID. Other compared identity fields are structurally present but not each independently corrupted.
findings.required_fix: Add one-bit fault injection for every response and loader tag field, especially window, order, sequence, source, half and bank mask.

findings.title: Post-abort recovery assumes reset also clears the macro models
findings.evidence: Recovery resets DUT and TB memory responders together. A selected physical macro may still return a pre-reset outstanding response unless reset/cancellation/drain semantics are explicitly defined.
findings.required_fix: Define selected-macro reset and outstanding-response semantics, then attack a late pre-abort response across reset.

findings.title: No physical or performance closure exists
findings.evidence: There is no full96 VCS, selected SRAM macro, DC/STA, activity power, energy or finite-trace cycle calibration. The 9.0x number is weight-read work and M238 1.687018x remains a model target.
findings.required_fix: Keep all speedup and PPA fields false until matched physical and finite-trace evidence exists.

allowed_claims: M241r2 repairs M241's fixed-one-cycle, overflow-success and loader-payload-binding failures for the tested standalone eight-lane checkpoint subset.
Exact VCS passes fixed 1/2/3 and deterministic varying 1-to-3 latency/stall schedules with 126 descriptors, 504 writes and 4,032 lane checks per mode at zero mismatch.
The tested stale weight-epoch and accumulator-payload responses are never accepted; the tested overflow produces no success commit or write, discards two younger tokens and recovers after reset.
The design retains lazy valid, a same-address interlock, zero accumulator forwarding payload and no M149 instance.
M259 independently proves complete response identity stability for the exercised weight and accumulator stall events using a review-only SVA overlay.
forbidden_claims: M241r2 formally proves arbitrary finite response latency
Every response or loader tag bit has an adversarial corruption test
M241r2 is full96 or a complete M152 trace
The 9.0x weight-read-work ratio is cycle or physical speedup
The M238 1.687018x target is admitted by M241r2
M241r2 proves DC/STA, energy, physical speedup, system speedup, paper PPA or a headline

next_gate.first: Correct the random/arbitrary-finite wording and promote complete response-tag stability into production SVA.
next_gate.second: Expand the tag fault matrix and test late responses across the selected macro's reset semantics.
next_gate.third: Only then extend to full96/full trace and matched physical closure.
